key_insight: The timing gap between two drop impacts determines whether their vortex rings merge symmetrically, merge imperfectly, or evolve independently.
engineering_relevance: For high-throughput mixing and droplet-based fluid systems, controlling impact synchronisation is critical to achieve predictable vortex formation and uniform mixing.
method: Two water drops were released onto a deep water pool with varying impact delays Δt.
Particle image velocimetry (PIV) was used to track the time evolution of the resulting vortex rings.
Observed ring interactions were grouped into four regimes based on Δt.
evidence_signal: Experiments identified four distinct interaction regimes, with thresholds near Δt < 0.5 ms, 0.5–7 ms, 7–80 ms, and Δt ≥ 80 ms.
watch_item: The regime boundaries are experiment-specific and depend on the droplet, pool, and wave conditions, so they may not transfer directly to other fluids or geometries.
paper_title: Interaction of vortex rings generated by two unsynchronised drop impacts
